common_name: Rainbow's End Miniature Rose (Yellow-to-Red-Edged Miniature Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container miniature roses in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Rainbow's End is one of the most widely grown miniature roses, ideal for a border edge, rock garden, or container.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Rainbow's End is a widely grown, award-winning miniature rose bearing small, high-centered double blooms that open golden-yellow and deepen to a red-edged blush as they age, giving a two-tone gradient effect across each flower and the whole plant. Its compact, bushy habit and continuous bloom from late spring through frost make it well suited to border edges, rock gardens, and containers where full-size roses would be out of scale. Like other miniature roses it needs the same full sun and regular feeding as its larger relatives, plus a preventative fungicide program in humid climates to manage black spot. Deadhead spent blooms to sustain the repeat-flowering habit, and prune back by about a third in late winter.
sources: American Rose Society — Miniature Rose Class
World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Jean Kenneally Miniature Rose (Apricot Blend Exhibition Miniature)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container miniature roses in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jean Kenneally is a favorite among exhibitors for its exceptionally well-formed, high-centered miniature blooms.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Jean Kenneally produces beautifully formed, high-centered, apricot-blend double blooms of exhibition quality on a taller-than-typical miniature rose plant, making it a favorite of miniature rose exhibitors as well as gardeners who want hybrid-tea-like flower form on a smaller scale. It reblooms reliably through the growing season and works well in a border, raised bed, or large container. As with other miniature roses, provide full sun and a preventative fungicide program to manage black spot in humid climates, and feed regularly through the growing season to support its continuous bloom. Deadhead spent flowers and prune back by about a third in late winter.
sources: American Rose Society — Miniature Rose Class
World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Gourmet Popcorn Miniature Rose (Fragrant Mounding White Miniature)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container miniature roses in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Gourmet Popcorn is an exceptionally floriferous, mounding miniature rose covered in small white flowers with a noticeable sweet fragrance, unusual for a mini.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Gourmet Popcorn is a sport of the earlier miniature rose Popcorn, valued for producing masses of small, semi-double white flowers with prominent gold stamens in large clusters that nearly cover the plant when in full bloom, plus a light, sweet fragrance that is stronger than most miniature roses offer. Its dense, mounding habit and heavy bloom make it an excellent choice for a low border edge, rock garden, or mass planting where a solid carpet of small white flowers is wanted. Give it full sun and a preventative fungicide program to keep black spot in check in humid climates, and deadhead or shear lightly after flushes to encourage continued bloom.
sources: American Rose Society — Miniature Rose Class
World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Black Jade Miniature Rose (Near-Black Deep Red Miniature)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container miniature roses in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Black Jade is prized among miniature rose growers for carrying some of the darkest flower color available in the class.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Black Jade bears small, high-centered, velvety near-black to deep blackish-red double blooms, among the darkest flower colors bred into any miniature rose, held on a compact, upright plant well suited to a container or small border. The intensely dark petals can be prone to sunburn in the most intense afternoon sun, so a site with a little relief from harsh midday exposure helps preserve flower quality. It reblooms through the growing season with regular feeding and deadheading. As with other miniature roses, a preventative fungicide program helps manage black spot in humid climates, and pruning back by about a third in late winter keeps the plant vigorous.
sources: American Rose Society — Miniature Rose Class
World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Starina Miniature Rose (Classic Orange-Red Exhibition Miniature)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container miniature roses in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Starina, introduced in 1965 by the French Meilland rose house, is one of the most celebrated and longest-cultivated miniature roses.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Starina, bred by the French Meilland rose house and introduced in 1965, bears perfectly formed, high-centered, brilliant orange-red double blooms that closely mimic full-size hybrid tea form in miniature scale, a combination that has made it one of the most enduringly popular and widely grown miniature roses ever introduced. Its vigorous, well-branched habit produces flowers continuously from late spring through frost, and it performs equally well in garden beds and containers. Provide full sun and a preventative fungicide program to manage black spot in humid climates, and deadhead spent blooms to sustain the long bloom season. Prune back by about a third in late winter.
sources: American Rose Society — Miniature Rose Class
World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Sun Sprinkles Miniature Rose (AARS-Winning Bright Yellow Miniature)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container miniature roses in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Sun Sprinkles is an All-America Rose Selections winner recognized for strong, clear yellow color and good disease resistance.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Sun Sprinkles was named an All-America Rose Selections winner for its clear, bright, non-fading golden-yellow double flowers with a light, sweet fragrance and notably good disease resistance for a miniature rose. Its compact, bushy habit produces continuous bloom from late spring through frost, making it a reliable choice for a border edge, container, or small bed. As with other miniature roses, give it full sun and regular feeding to sustain its heavy bloom, and keep an eye on black spot in humid climates even though it shows better-than-average resistance. Deadhead spent flowers and prune back by about a third in late winter.
sources: American Rose Society — Miniature Rose Class
